plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning and paying more than the item is worth to me; if I bid lower, I risk losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $18, I will bid exactly $18.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, and underbidding risks losing a profitable auction. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, and since this is a one-shot game, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid regardless of your own bid (as long as you're highest). Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth if you win against a bid between your value and your bid; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since this is a single round with no repeated learning needed, I will bid exactly my true value of $21 to maximize expected profit.
